title: geogen glTF node extras, version 1
description: Gameplay metadata geogen writes to glTF node extras under the 'geogen' key. This file is the whole contract: the exporter writes a node meta key only when it is declared here (src/geogen/extras.py; build-only keys are registered there and never exported), so 'geogen' takes no other keys. runtime/godot/README.md lists which runtime script reads each key.

x-godot.for: warns once when it isn't the supported version

version.description: The version of this contract the node was written to.

x-godot.for: the stable ID: `node_by_uid`, event subjects, saved state

uid.description: Stable ID: '<package>:<authored path>' (cottage:house/door), from the names things were authored with, never the exported node name. Present on placed assets and scenes, tagged or typed nodes and anything with interactions. Content and saved state refer to nodes by it, so it survives a re-export; <name>.refs.json beside the manifest lists every one.

x-godot.for: node groups (`furniture.bed` and `furniture`)

tags.description: Semantic tags, dotted from general to specific (room, room.hotel_bedroom, furniture.bed, door.interior).

x-godot.for: what kind of node it is: `room_volume`, `place`, `spawn`, `npc`, `traffic`, `train`, `light`, `lod`, `collider`

type.description: Special node kinds. room_volume: axis-aligned box (in the node's frame) of size 'size' centred on the node. spawn: player start, facing the node's +Z. collider: collision-only geometry (Godot suffix -colonly = trimesh, -convcolonly = convex); do not render. material_group: helper node whose primitives were folded into its parent's mesh (left unreferenced). npc: a character placed here (see 'npc'); its body asset is the child named by npc.body.node. vehicle: a vehicle asset root (see 'vehicle'). place: a named trigger volume (see 'place'). light: the <node>_light child carrying a fixture's KHR_lights_punctual light. lod: a <node>_LOD<n> level of its parent's mesh (see 'level', 'ratio'). traffic: the root of a moving fleet (see 'fleet'); its children are the starting vehicles. train: a train (see 'train'); its children are the consist.

x-godot.for: collider nodes: convex (`box`, `hull`) or trimesh

shape.description: Collider nodes only: how the collision geometry was made.

x-godot.for: only to tell mesh parts from things in `world.node`

collider.description: Mesh nodes: the collider chosen for this mesh (none = no collision). The collider itself is a child node.

x-godot.for: `<node>_LOD<n>` nodes; the runtime drops them and uses Godot's own LODs

level.description: type lod only: the LOD level, 1 = the first reduction (the node is named <node>_LOD<level>).

x-godot.for: `<node>_LOD<n>` nodes; the runtime drops them and uses Godot's own LODs

ratio.description: type lod only: the share of the full mesh's triangles this level was decimated to.

x-godot.for: as `collider`; the navmesh is baked from colliders

walkable.description: Surface meant to be walked on (navmesh input).

room.description: Room identity, on room nodes and their room_volume.

door.description: Door/opening nodes generated by floor plans.

x-godot.for: a floor-plan door's hinge (the door's interaction is what moves it)

joint.description: Articulation pivot (e.g. a door leaf's hinge): children rotate about 'axis' (node frame) between min_deg and max_deg.

x-godot.for: body animations and transition clips

clips.description: Skeletal animation clips over the joints below this node. Each is a glTF animation named 'animation' (<node>_<clip>; engines may mangle '/') targeting the joint nodes (Skeleton3D bones in Godot); 'loop' clips repeat.

speed.description: Locomotion clips: the ground speed (m/s) the cycle was made for; scale playback by actual speed / this.

rests.description: Pose clips: the hands (IK end bones) resting on a support in this pose, a table top or a sill, made for a default height: a runtime may move them onto the support that is really there.

leap.description: Jump clips (one-shots): the body's way from where it takes off to where it lands while the clip plays, sampled at 'times' (s): across by 'run' (share) of the level way between the two, up by 'rise' (share) of the climb or drop and 'lift' m more. Interpolate linearly between samples.

from.description: Transition clips (sit_down, stand_up, ...): the pose the clip starts in.

to.description: Transition clips: the pose the clip ends in. Play the clip when changing pose from 'from' to 'to'.

root.description: Transition clips: the body root's path while the clip plays, in the frame of where the character ends up (the affordance anchor; the approach point when 'to' is stand), x right, y up, z forward. Made for the action's default approach offset and seat height: blend the difference to the actual start and end placements over the clip.

x-godot.for: a `GeogenInteraction` (`scripts/interaction.gd`) each

interactions.description: Asset nodes: state machines that move descendant nodes (by exported node name). Exported transforms show the 'initial' state; a part's rest pose is M(initial value)^-1 * its exported transform, and its pose for value v is asset * M(v) * rest, where M rotates by v degrees about 'axis' through 'pivot' (asset frame) or translates v metres along 'axis'. use() goes to states[target].next; 'then' auto-advances on arrival; 'emit' names an event raised on arrival.

targets.description: Nodes the player aims at to use it.

refused.description: What the prompt says, and a refused use tells the user, while the interaction's `when` (in the manifest's state) is false.

reach.description: Metres from the eye its targets can be used from, when that is further than the player's reach (absent: the player's).

touch.description: The grip point (`grips`) a body touches to work it: an NPC's `use:` step presses it with the `press` motion, and the state changes when the finger gets there.

lock.description: While locked, use() fails; holders of 'key' can lock/unlock.

after.description: Dwell before 'then' (auto-close): seconds, or {minutes: n} of clock time (the rules program moves it on).

type.description: rotate: values in degrees about axis through pivot; translate: metres along axis; visible: 1 shown, 0 hidden (with their colliders), no axis or pivot; drive: values are the target speed (deg/s or m/s) of the motor on mechanism body 'body' (this node's 'mechanism'), eased in and out over the interaction's duration, a missing state 0 (a brake), the motor off in the 'free' states; states in 'to' send the joint to a position instead ('at': metres along a slide, degrees round a hinge, from the exported pose) at up to that state's 'speed', speeding up and slowing down at 'accel', and are reached when the body is there; no nodes.

footprint.description: Furniture: floor footprint [x, z] in metres (asset frame, centred on the origin).

clearance.description: Furniture: free space needed beyond the footprint on each side (front = +Z), metres.

x-godot.for: tunes the fixture's imported light; `auto: night`

light.description: Light fixtures: an omni light at 'offset' (node frame). Exported as a KHR_lights_punctual point light on a <node>_light child (intensity = energy * 12 cd).

auto.description: night: switched by the runtime's world clock (on after dark), not by a switch.

x-godot.for: particles from the part, switched by its `running` state

emitter.description: Particles the part gives off, described physically (geogen.emitters). offset: metres in the part's frame; rate: particles/s; lifetime: s; speed: [min, max] m/s; direction: unit vector in the part's frame; spread: degrees; gravity: m/s^2 downward (negative rises); wind: m/s^2 in the world frame; drag: m/s lost per second; size: [birth, death] m across; area: emission box in m; running: how the part's `running` state starts.

x-godot.for: a synthesised loop at the part, switched by its `running` state

sound.description: A synthesised looping sound at the part (geogen.emitters): noise in band [low, high] Hz, a hum in Hz (0: none), flutter and crackle 0-1, heard out to range metres; offset in the part's frame; running: how the part's `running` state starts.

x-godot.for: sit / lie / use points for the player and NPCs

affordances.description: Things an actor can do at an asset (asset frame): sit/lie/use/stand/look at 'position' facing 'yaw' degrees about +Y (0 = +Z); 'height' is where the hips rest. The player takes sit/lie; NPCs run 'action' (assets/npcs/actions.yaml), starting from 'approach' (floor level), for 'duration' seconds, adding 'advertises' to their needs (after 'takes' and 'gives': what it does to what the actor carries, offered only when 'requires' holds); 'slots' actors at once; 'interaction' is the asset interaction a use step drives.

depth.description: sit: how far in front of 'position' the seat's front edge is, metres. With the body pose's 'reach' it keeps the sitter's calves clear of the seat.

body.description: A body of this node's 'mechanism' the seat is part of: a seated player rides with it.

requires.description: What doing it needs: 'holding' an item the actor carries (any of these ids), 'state' this node's interactions showing these states. Not offered otherwise; NPCs plan chains of affordances that meet it.

near.description: The nearest thing with this tag in front of the place, within `within` m, must show these states.

takes.description: Done, it takes one of the first of these items the actor carries (item ids).

gives.description: Done, the actor carries these more: {item id: count}.

sets.description: Done, this node's interactions go to these states: {interaction: state}.

uses.description: Other things done at the same place, by name: each is an affordance of its own to NPCs (id '<node>#<index>.<name>') with these in place of the affordance's, sharing where it is, its action (unless it names its own) and its slots (a chair is a seat, and with a meal in hand somewhere to eat it).

action.description: Its own action (assets/npcs/actions.yaml) in place of the affordance's: a chair's eat.

interaction.description: Its own interaction of this node, in place of the affordance's.

near.description: The nearest thing with this tag in front of the place, within `within` m, must show these states.

x-godot.for: doorways NPC paths open (`scripts/npc.gd`)

portal.description: A doorway NPC paths may cross (asset frame): width x height opening centred on 'center', 'depth' thick along 'normal'. A path through it while 'interaction' isn't in state 'open' runs the NPC 'pass' action (stop 'clearance' beyond the near face, open, walk through, maybe close).

swing.description: The side the leaf opens toward: front (+normal) or back.

handles.description: The handle on each side (front: +normal), its middle in the asset frame as the door stands when exported. An NPC reaches for the one on its side to open the door; on the side the leaf swings away from it stands close enough to hold it as it opens.

x-godot.for: `PlaceArea` trigger volumes

place.description: type place only: a named trigger volume (geogen/places.py). The node is the middle of the volume's bottom and the volume rises along its +Y: a box of 'size' [x, y, z], or the footprint 'polygon' ([x, z] points in the node's frame) extruded 'height'. Actors (the player, NPCs) entering and leaving it are events whose subject is the node's uid.

detect.description: What the place reports, when not only actors: with 'props', physics props in it count too, and the runtime keeps its 'occupants' state (the number of things in it).

sink.description: Spawned items (geogen/flows.py) entering it are taken in: only those named in 'accepts' (empty: any). The runtime keeps its 'received' state (how many) and raises 'received' {item, ...the item's data}.

x-godot.for: rigid-body props, carrying, spawn / stow

physics.description: A physics prop (geogen/physics.py): the node and everything under it are one rigid body, a box of 'size' centred at 'center' (the node's frame), or with 'shape' a sphere of 'radius' or an upright capsule of 'radius' and 'height' (end to end) centred there. 'damping' slows it (linear, angular: per second). The parts' own colliders are not used. 'carry': the player can pick it up. 'spawn_at' (the node's frame): where its 'spawn' interaction puts it on going live; stowed, it is hidden and out of the simulation, and a live prop that falls out of the world is stowed.

x-godot.for: jointed rigid bodies with motors (rides); `drive` motions in `interaction.gd` run the motors

mechanism.description: A mechanism (geogen/mechanism.py): the asset's parts in 'nodes' (exported names) form rigid bodies, one per entry, each held by its 'joint' to body 'to' (absent: the world) at 'pivot' (the asset's frame): a 'hinge' turns about 'axis', a 'slide' moves along it, within 'limits' (degrees or metres from the exported pose) when given; a 'pin' is a ball joint; a 'swing' turns about 'axis' (level) and about the level line across it, never about the vertical (a chair on chains). 'damping' (per second) is a damper in the joint, on its own motion (a swing dies down). 'motor' is a motor on a hinge or slide the node's interactions run with 'drive' motions: 'speed' deg/s or m/s, 'force' the most it pushes with (N·m or N). Bodies collide as the convex hulls of their parts' colliders; the two bodies a joint holds don't collide with each other; the asset's other parts are static.

limits.description: [lo, hi] for a hinge (degrees) or slide (metres); for a swing, the furthest it swings either way (degrees).

x-godot.for: spawned items: a source's rate, limits and spawn point

flows.description: Spawned items (geogen/flows.py). 'track': see below. 'source': this asset makes copies of the item templates among its descendants (nodes with 'item') while it runs: 'rate' a second, and at once for each one its 'queued' state asks for, while it has fewer than 'max_alive' in the world and has made fewer than 'count' (0: no limit). They appear at 'at' (this node's frame), up to 'spread' m off it across x and z, physics items moving at 'velocity' (this node's frame). Its state: running, queued (rules set them), emitted and alive (the runtime drives them); signal emitted {item}.

items.description: What it makes: none yet for a waves source built alone (its waves are read when it is placed).

item.description: The item file, relative to assets/.

name.description: The item's name: its template's 'item.name' (absent: the asset was built alone, with no templates).

order.description: Its place among the scene's sources (by position: the order they are stepped in).

track.description: The order of the track whose start is within 0.5 m of 'at': it puts its items on it (absent: none).

waves.description: Instead of items at a rate: while running, wave by wave. A wave starts 'delay' s after the source runs; its groups go out in order, 'count' items of 'name' each 'gap' s apart; when all of the wave's items are gone it is cleared (signal wave_cleared {wave}), and the source stops (running false) unless 'auto'. After the last, all_cleared. State 'wave' counts them. A file name: the asset was built alone (no waves read).

effector.description: Acts on track items in 'range' m of 'at' (this node's frame), 'rate' times a second while its 'enabled' state is true: 'effect' damage (items with data.hp lose that much; at 0 they are destroyed and their source raises killed {item, ...data}) or take (the item goes; its 'taken' state counts, signal took). 'targets': first (furthest along), last, nearest, strongest (most hp); 'accepts' limits it to those items. 'aim' parts (exported node names) turn toward the target, yaw about their Y and pitch about their X, 'turn_rate' deg/s; 'projectile' is what a shot looks like (damage lands as it fires).

order.description: Its place among the scene's effectors (by position: the order they act in).

track.description: A path items follow: 'points' (this node's frame, every 0.25 m) 'length' m long. belt: items move at 'speed' together and queue; walk: each at its own item speed; roll: gravity drives each from 'speed' ((5/7) g sin(slope), less 'damping' per second), and they spin (physics items too: they fall off a 'drop' end as bodies). Items keep 'spacing' (or their radii) apart. 'end': auto (on to the track whose start is within 0.5 m of this end, else a sink), sink (take them in: 'received' state and signal, only 'accepts' items when listed), stop (they wait there), drop (they fall off as physics bodies). A source whose spawn point is within 0.5 m of a track's start puts its items on it. Its state: running (inputs start / stop), received.

order.description: Its place among the scene's tracks (by position: the order they are stepped in), from the whole scene's network (geogen/flows.py network).

next.description: 'end: auto': the order of the track whose start is within 0.5 m of this end (absent: none, it is a sink).

x-godot.for: an item's body under the hidden `item_icons` node: taken out of the world on load and rendered into the HUD hotbar's icon for that item (`item_icons()`)

item_icon.description: An item's body for a runtime's inventory to draw (geogen/inventory.py attach_icons): a child of the hidden 'item_icons' node, not part of the world (the runtime takes it out on load). 'item' is the item's id (items/<id>.yaml).

held.description: Shown in an actor's hand while it carries the item (geogen.87.2): the body on 'bone' (a skeleton bone), placed by 'offset' (m) and 'rotation' (deg, XYZ) in the hand's frame (y along the fingers, z out of the palm, x forward).

x-godot.for: an item template: taken out of the world on load and copied by its source

item.description: An item template (geogen/flows.py): not part of the world (the runtime takes it out on load) but what its source copies. 'mode': physics (a rigid body, from this node's 'physics'), belt or walk (along a track). 'data' is what each copy carries; 'lifetime' and 'stuck' (s) take a copy away (0: never). 'gait' is how a walk item's body steps: it bobs 'bob' m twice a 'stride' (m), rocks 'sway' degrees side to side and swings its heading 'waddle' degrees.

held.description: Shown in an actor's hand while it carries the item (geogen.87.2): the body on 'bone' (a skeleton bone), placed by 'offset' (m) and 'rotation' (deg, XYZ) in the hand's frame (y along the fingers, z out of the palm, x forward).

x-godot.for: travel points

travel.description: A travel point (geogen/travel.py): 'use' it (its 'travel' interaction emits 'travel') or walk into 'volume' (asset frame, on: enter) to go to spawn 'spawn' (default: the first) of catalogue scene 'scene' (absent: this scene). 'target' names the part aimed at for on: use.

x-godot.for: on body assets; NPCs read the copy in `npc.body.poses`

poses.description: Character body assets: named poses as root transforms relative to an anchor (offset m, rotation deg XYZ, scale).

x-godot.for: binding a motion's roles to points on this thing (a mug's handle, a table's top)

grips.description: Things a body touches: the asset's attachments that say how (`grip:` hook, pinch, press, put, sit, ...), in order, each in the node's own frame ([tx, ty, tz, qx, qy, qz, qw]; geogen/motion.py grip_points). A motion role with `grip: any` binds the first a hand holds it by.

x-godot.for: running motions (motions.json) on this body

rig.description: Character bodies: what a motion rig (geogen/motion.py, scripts/motion_rig.gd) poses the skeleton with. Bones in hierarchy order with their rest in the parent's frame ([tx, ty, tz, qx, qy, qz, qw]; a rig poses relative to these, not to an engine's import rest), the skeleton's params (the values `{expr}` in motions read), its channels and hand shapes (left-hand bones in body-frame degrees, mirrored), the pose library (each pose's rotations relative to rest, [x, y, z, w], and offsets, m) and where each posture puts the body (`root_poses`). Transition clips (sit_down) are the body's exported animations, listed with their root paths in `clips`.

root_poses.description: Where each posture puts the body against what it is at (a beat's `root: {at, posture}`): offset (m) and rotation (deg XYZ), the body asset's `poses`.

x-godot.for: a `GeogenNpc` (`scripts/npc.gd`) from the resolved definition

npc.description: A placed NPC, fully resolved from assets/npcs/<definition>.yaml: everything the runtime interpreter needs. Distances in metres, rates per second. 'home.polygon' is [x, z] in this node's frame.

character.description: A named person's character file (assets/people/<character>.yaml, kind: character); 'definition' is then its role.

name.description: A named person's name, for labels, prompts and dialogue.

body.description: The body: an 'asset' file or a character 'archetype' (with the person drawn as 'character'), built with 'params', placed as the child 'node'; 'poses' are its root transforms per pose.

urgent.description: Below this level the need's shortfall counts 'boost' times more when choosing what to do.

at_zero.description: When the need runs out: 'action' is run where the NPC stands, and gives 'recover' of the need back.

planner.description: The NPC decides by plans: chains of affordances found through what they require, take and give (geogen/planner.py; scripts/npc_planner.gd). 'depth': the longest chain; 'patience': seconds added to a chain's time when scoring it; 'nodes': the search's limit; 'hands': the most it carries at once, and it commits to one run of a plan at a time so others can share the job.

skips.description: Affordances carrying one of these tags are left to someone else.

offers.description: What other NPCs may do with this one (talk): each is an option 'with/<this NPC's stable ID>/<name>' to an NPC that has this one within its home. Both are held for each other while it lasts; the one who chose it runs 'action' (its 'go_to: partner' walks up, 'wait: duration' is the time together), this one runs 'answer' if it is on its feet (seated, it stays and looks at them), and both get 'advertises'.

relations.description: How well it knows the others, 0..1 each: it starts at 'household' for NPCs with its 'household' and 'stranger' for the rest, and doing an offer together adds 'grow'. An offer's score is multiplied by 0.5 + how well it knows the one offering; a seat beside one it knows 'friend' or better is liked as one beside a groupmate.

life.description: What stays changed about a person (geogen.111). 'practice' grows by what they finish doing (the tags in 'from', 'per_use' each); 'chapters' are the stretches of their life in order: entering one applies its 'becomes' for good (preferences, need keys, 'home' rects in world metres joined to their home), moves every interaction named in 'tends' to that state and writes 'story' in their story; 'pursues' makes things with a tag worth that much to them; when everything in 'until' holds (practice levels, how well they know someone, an interaction's state) the next chapter starts.

x-godot.for: `GeogenLife`

household.description: The people it lives with: NPCs with the same name know each other from the start ('relations').

cooldown.description: Seconds after doing it before it is an option again.

visit.description: A key of 'visits': the region its action's 'go_to: visit' goes to.

visits.description: Places outside the home its activities' 'visit' makes short trips to: {name: {polygon, y}} in the node's frame, like 'home'.

owns.description: Stable IDs of the things only this NPC uses (an affordance under one is refused to others); it likes them best.

prefers.description: Stable IDs of things it likes best (an affordance under one scores higher), still free for others.

work.description: Stable ID of where its routine's 'at: work' blocks keep it: their options are the affordances under it, wherever that is from home.

group.description: People who came together (a scatter's group): 'leader' is the stable ID of the group's leader (the leader's own for itself), 'radius' how near a groupmate counts as together (m). Its 'together' need refills within the radius and decays apart; 'go_to: group' walks a member to the leader and the leader to its nearest member; an affordance on the same thing as, or beside, one a groupmate holds scores higher.

affordance_tags.description: Only affordances with one of these tags (empty: any).

wander.description: Where go_to: random goes: points on up-facing surfaces of nodes with these tags (empty: the home region).

routine.description: Time-of-day blocks ('from' / 'to' in hours, wrapping midnight): while one is active its 'activities' and 'preferences' multiply scores, and 'away' sends the NPC off (the leave action) until it ends.

at.description: work: the block's options are the affordances under the NPC's 'work'.

only.description: Affordance tags ('owns': the NPC's own things): the block's options are only affordances with one of them, none of its activities (all of them if none is free).

hold.description: The NPC stays on the affordance it takes (its wait on 'duration') until the block ends: in its bed all night.

quests.description: Ids of the quests the NPC is given when the block starts (the export's rules do that, and repeat them); it works on them only while the block lasts.

wants.description: Conditions on the world it puts right with whatever is there (geogen/npc.py WANT_KEYS), by name. 'of' is what a want is about (prop: a physics prop with carry); 'when' says which are a problem (resting_on: floor, anything actors walk on); 'action' runs with that subject and a place the runtime finds among the spots that hold it within reach, scored by 'place' (its tags' 'prefer' multipliers, less 'distance' per metre walked, less 'off_height' per metre from the 'height' above its feet it likes, less 'tried' for a spot already used for the subject, plus 'noise' x random; 'radius' m round it where it has no home). Utility: 'weight' plus what 'advertises' adds for its needs, less 'reluctance' for each time this NPC has picked the subject up (for any reason; a handling fades over 'forget' s); a subject whose reluctance has used up the weight is left be. A want about things ('of' a reference, resolved at export into 'subjects') is unhappy with each subject whose interaction shows 'when.state' (with 'when.room': empty, only while no character is in the room volume the thing is in) and runs 'action' to bring it to 'to'; operating a subject is a handling.

of.description: prop, or the reference a want about things was written with (the runtime uses 'subjects').

to.description: A want about things: the state its action brings a subject's interaction to.

subjects.description: A want about things: the things 'of' names in this scene, by stable ID, each with the interaction the want is about.

quality.description: Weights for qualities of a spot, each 0..1 and added to its score times the weight: high, enclosed, hidden and warm are worked out from the world (geogen/npc.py PLACE_QUALITIES); a thing tagged quality.<name> gives its spots that quality (soft, warm, any other name).

senses.description: What it can notice (geogen/npc.py SENSES_DEFAULTS); a part left out is a sense it lacks. hearing: a stimulus carries 'range' m x its loudness x its strength, and only 'muffled' of that with something in the way. sight: within 'range' m and a 'cone' of degrees ahead, with a clear line.

reacts.description: The stimuli it reacts to (assets/npcs/stimuli.yaml, inlined), by name. A stimulus is a bus 'event' (impact: a physics prop hit something; changed: an interaction went to another state), from a subject tagged 'of' if given, heard as far as 'loudness' of the hearing range. Noticing one (never its own doing), the head turns to it for 'look' s, and with 'interrupt' an interruptible action is cut short so it decides again.

memory.description: With memory, its wants about props know only the props it has seen (where, and what they rested on) or heard land (a stimulus it reacts to: where the noise was), each for 'forget' s after it last perceived it; it looks round every 'every' s, and forgets a remembered thing it can see is no longer where it was. One only heard of, or not where it was, it first goes to look for with the 'search' action.

reach.description: What the body's hands get to: no further than 'distance' m on the ground from where it stands, between the 'heights' [lo, hi] m above its feet; 'stand' is how far short of a prop it stops to pick it up.

jump.description: What its body can jump (geogen.100.6), m: 'up' onto something at most this much higher, 'down' off something at most this much higher, 'across' as far as this level. Spots off the navmesh (perches) are reached by a jump from a navmesh point within reach, and left by a jump down; the body plays its 'jump_up' / 'jump_down' clip and follows the clip's 'leap'. Absent: it doesn't jump.

carry.description: The physics props it can carry: at most 'mass' kg and 'size' m on the longest side. One over 'two_hands' m on its longest side is carried in front of the body in both hands, a smaller one in one hand.

attention.description: How it notices the player (geogen/npc.py ATTENTION_DEFAULTS); a part left out is off. look: head look-at within 'range' m and a 'cone' of degrees, turning up to 'yaw' / 'pitch' degrees at 'speed'. greet: on E it raises 'signal' (not twice within 'debounce' s) and, standing, runs 'action' (waving at most every 'cooldown' s), looking at the greeter 'acknowledge' s. yield: steps 'step' m aside ('action') from a player walking at it within 'distance' m.

interruptible.description: Something the NPC notices (reacts: interrupt) may cut this action short: it skips to the step that stands it up again, or ends.

container.description: Storage: how many items it holds, and which part is the storage volume.

x-godot.for: rooms the playtest shouldn't expect to reach

nav.description: false on rooms/room volumes that aren't meant to be walked (lift shafts); playtests skip them.

size.description: room_volume only: box size in metres [x, y, z].

city.description: City district root (geogen/layout/city.py): the block grid and the district's extent in metres.

block.description: City block: its grid index [i, j].

lot.description: City lot: the block it is in, its zone, the block side it fronts and its rectangle [x0, z0, x1, z1] in the city frame.

building.description: A building root: its storey count and height in metres. A building a city placed on a lot also has the catalogue 'entry' it was drawn from (a recipe name or asset file stem) and its 'zone'.

street_furniture.description: Kind of street furniture: lamp, tree, bench, hydrant, ...

x-godot.for: root of a chunk's LOD stand-in (the streamer works from the chunk index)

lod.description: Root of a chunk's exterior LOD stand-in: decimated to 'ratio' of its triangles, parts smaller than 'min_size' metres dropped.

x-godot.for: root of a chunk's interior (the streamer works from the chunk index)

interior.description: Root of a streamed building interior chunk: the building (by name) it belongs to.

x-godot.for: signal heads lit from their intersection's cycle (with `crossing`: pedestrian heads, lit from that pedestrian signal)

signal.description: A traffic signal head: the intersection and phase it shows and the lane it faces (ids of the manifest's traffic section). The runtime lights its lamp_red | lamp_amber | lamp_green parts from that intersection's cycle. With 'crossing' it is a pedestrian head: the runtime lights lamp_walk or lamp_dont from that entry of the traffic section's pedestrian_signals.

crossing.description: Pedestrian heads: the id of the pedestrian signal (a crosswalk's walk and clearance intervals) they show.

character.description: A person drawn from a character archetype (geogen/characters.py): the archetype (a '/'-joined chain when variants hand the draw on) and the seed that picked them.

x-godot.for: the `NavigationLink3D` and walking path of a spiral stair

stairs.description: A flight of stairs (geogen/generators/stairs.py). Spiral stairs add 'ends', where you step on at the bottom and off at the top (node frame): a runtime should link them on its navigation map, since a self-overlapping spiral's navmesh comes out in pieces; 'path' is the walking line between them, for bodies that follow the link.

x-godot.for: parameters of `scripts/water.gdshader`

water.description: A water sheet (geogen/generators/water.py): what a water shader needs; every key is optional and a runtime has its own defaults. Colours are linear RGB.

depth_scale.description: Depth in metres over which shallow turns to deep.

x-godot.for: where a fleet vehicle starts on the lane graph

driving.description: A vehicle of a moving fleet (a child of a type traffic node): where it starts on the lane graph. 'lane' is a lane id of the manifest's traffic section, 's' metres along it, 'factor' this driver's share of the lane speed.

x-godot.for: a `GeogenTraffic` (`scripts/traffic.gd`)

fleet.description: type traffic only: how its vehicles drive (geogen/traffic.py, from a kind: traffic definition). 'count' vehicles, 'spacing' metres apart at the start; 'driving' is the IDM car-following model; 'turns' weights the choice at intersections; 'yield' lists who they stop for; 'schedule' is [[hour, share of the fleet on the road], ...] over the day.

headway.description: Seconds kept behind the vehicle ahead.

give_up.description: Seconds held on green before picking another exit.

x-godot.for: a `GeogenTrain` (`scripts/train.gd`)

train.description: type train only: a train and its precomputed run (geogen/trains.py). 'railway' is a railway id of the manifest's traffic.railways. 'run' is the distance along the line of the train's middle every 'dt' seconds for one departure ('duration' seconds long); departures repeat every timetable.headway from timetable.offset. 'stops' are when it stands at each station and 'closures' the [from, to] times each level crossing is shut, all in seconds from departure. 'cars' are the consist (child node names), each 'offset' metres from the train's middle with its bogie pivots (z in the car's frame).

warning.description: Seconds a crossing closes before the train reaches it.

x-godot.for: wheels, lamps, clearance, sound

vehicle.description: A vehicle asset (geogen/vehicles.py), built along +Z with its origin on the ground midway between the axles. Parts named here are descendants of this node: wheels spin about their local X (radius in metres), steer parts turn, paint parts carry the tint, lamps glow by kind. clearance is [length, width, height]; front/rear are the bumper z positions.

bogie_centers.description: Rail: z of each bogie's pivot (vehicle frame).

sound.description: Synthesised sound hooks: engine {base Hz, per_speed Hz per m/s, volume_db, roughness}, horn {tones Hz, seconds, volume_db}.

params.description: An asset's params, as it was built with them: a map, not a fixed set of keys (each asset declares its own).

npc_step.description: One step of an NPC action (assets/npcs/actions.yaml): exactly one verb, with options 'at' (where a pose is held), 'hold' (a pose step: the skeletal pose clip pose_<hold> to hold instead of the pose's own, where the body has it), 'loop' (a play step: loop the clip for that long, 'duration' being the affordance's range), 'close' (a go_to step: past the navmesh path, step straight up to the target when it is near and clear: a counter), 'look' (where the head turns from this step on, until a later step says otherwise or the action ends: the action's subject, place or anchor) and 'if' (a flag it needs). go_to 'nearby' is a random navmesh point a few metres from where the NPC stands.

do.description: Run this motion (motions.json) on the body and wait for it to end; a body with no rig, or an export without the motion, goes straight on.

roles.description: A do step: what the motion's roles are bound to.

params.description: A do step: the motion's params ('duration': drawn from the action's range).

keep.description: A do step: start the motion and go on; it runs until the option ends.

pick_up.description: Take the action's subject (a physics prop with carry) in hand: the NPC must stand within its reach, and the prop be within its carry limits.

put_down.description: Let the prop in hand go just above the action's place; where it settles is the physics' business.

find.description: The nearest free affordance of these types the NPC may use (in its home, not another's, not reserved, nothing on it) becomes the action's anchor, approach and heading; pose 'found' takes its pose (sit, lie). Nothing free: the action goes on where it is.

part.description: A wait: duration step's share of the duration, drawn once for the action (eating in stages).

set_out.description: Put the carried item's body (items/<id>.yaml body) on what is in front of the NPC (a table) until the action ends or the item is used up.

show.description: {item: state}: that carried item's body, in the hand or set out, shows a state of its own interaction (a meal: full, half, empty).

prefer.description: A find step's {tag: factor}: how far a thing with that tag counts (below 1: preferred).

use_item.description: Use an item the NPC carries, as the player's F does (the rules' use_item event with the NPC as the actor): an item id, or "[tag=<tag>]" for the first carried item with that tag.

reach.description: sit: z of the back of the calves below the seat, relative to the anchor, metres (compare an affordance's 'depth').
